quote: 1. When you sell half, if the stock goes higher you say to yourself, 'Thank goodness I kept half.' If the stock goes lower, you'll say, 'Thank goodness I sold half.' Psychologically, it's a win/win either way.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 2. You need to be decisive, open-minded, flexible and competitive.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 3. I put a lot more weight into how this stock is acting relative to the S&P — you can see real divergences when stocks are making new highs and the relative strength line is not.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 4. Don't bet big unless a) you love your thesis, and b) you're hot.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 5. There really is no intelligent reason to increase your trading size if your positions are showing losses.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 6. The higher the relative strength the better. Once the relative strength starts falling off, I usually get out of the stock.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 7. I think contrarianism is overrated. Soros used to say the crowd's right 80% of the time. You just can't be caught in the other 20% because you can get your head handed to you. I get some intellectual satisfaction out of playing in the 20%, but as a concept, I think contrarianism is overrated.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 9. If I get stopped out, I get stopped out. I don't think, I just get out.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 11. I think a lot of my performance has been because I'm flexible in terms of the assets I use. I'm not afraid to just play in bonds or currencies or this or that.

quote: 14. You can get so focused on the results that you don't do what you should be doing.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 15. I always try to keep losses very small. 7 per cent is a great percentage to use.

quote: 16. In the stock market, you can make money or you can make excuses, but you can't make both. Do whatever it takes to eliminate your own personal excuses. Your road to success starts by taking responsibility.

quote: 17. Never stray from the basics of rule number one of always going in with a plan.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 18. The market keeps teaching the same lesson to every serious practitioner who is willing to listen.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 19. One of the reasons of my success was open mindedness to various asset classes. It gives you the discipline to not play when you shouldn't be playing.

quote: 20. You must not risk more than you can reasonably expect to gain; otherwise, you're stacking the odds against you, and that's gambling.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 22. If you try to learn from every single trade that you make, you are only going to get better and better as time goes on.

quote: 23. If you find yourself getting stopped out of your positions over and over, there can only be two things wrong: 1. Your stock selection criteria are flawed. 2. The general market environment is hostile.

quote: 24. It's not enough to have knowledge, a dream, or passion; it's what you do with what you know that counts. The best time to get started is now!

quote: 27. My goal is just to become a better and better trader, more and more disciplined, so I can be more and more successful in the market. I am disciplined in implementing the system and sticking to it.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 28. With every trade I make, my approach is always 'risk-first.' By thinking and acting 'risk-first,' you know exactly what you stand to lose if you're wrong, which in trading is far more important than what you stand to gain if you're right.

quote: 29. If you want to make money in the market, if you want to be successful in anything, you really got to put in a lot of time.

quote: 30. My longevity stems from the fact that I try to control risk as much as possible. When the market starts down I sell quickly and don't let the losses get out of hand.

quote: 31. I'm always thinking about losing money as opposed to making money. Don't focus on making money, focus on protecting what you have.

quote: 32. I believe the best way to manage risk is to be bullish when you have a compelling risk/reward and bearish when you don't.

quote: 33. The market is the greatest humbling device in the world.

quote: 34. Unrequited love in the stock market can be very expensive.

quote: 35. A loss never bothers me after I take it. I might be wrong on a stock more than once in a row, but I'm not going to be wrong for very long.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 36. You want to be involved in a stock while it is undergoing accumulation, not distribution.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 37. You should not risk more than you expect to gain on average; I call that the 'Cardinal Sin.'

quote: 38. If you normally cut losses at 7 to 8 percent, cut them at 5 to 6 percent.

quote: 39. My percentage of winners is only about 50/50, because I cut my losers very quickly.

quote: 40. With each buy order I enter, I know the exact price where I am going to sell at a loss if things don't work out as expected. I define this price level before I get in.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 41. Everyone makes mistakes; that's unavoidable. But not correcting a mistake or minimizing the damage of a position gone wrong is completely under your own control. quote: 42. If it reenters its base, I have a rule to cut at least 50 percent of the position.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 43. I'm only rich because I know when I'm wrong.

quote: 44. Growth comes at the expense of comfort.

quote: 45. There is a lot more noise and movement in the market with high speed trading and computerized algorithms, but the stocks that have the biggest moves continue to have the same characteristics.

quote: 46. I've never made a buy at a low that I didn't just feel terrible and scared to death making it. It's easy to sell at the bottom. You can go home that night and it relieves you of your nerves.

quote: 47. It's better to lose correctly than to win incorrectly.

quote: 48. I usually hold my big winners for about six to twelve months, stocks that aren't that strong about three months, and my losers less than two weeks.

quote: 49. Hope is not a strategy.

quote: 50. Those who succeed big at anything all have the same attitude: You keep going until it happens or you die trying. Quitting is not an option.

quote: 52. The biggest mistake investors make is they invest in the present rather than forward looking and looking at where the puck is going instead of where the puck is.

quote: 53. You want to get on board when institutional money is pouring into a stock and lifting it significantly higher.

quote: 54. Figuring yourself out and developing a discipline are probably the most important things.

quote: 55. I've learned many things from George Soros, but perhaps the most significant is that it's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 56. It's like studying an animal; certain stocks have certain characteristics and a certain way of behaving. You need to recognize when those characteristics are changing and act accordingly.

quote: 57. What I learned from George Soros was sizing is 70 or 80 percent of the equation.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 58. Earnings don't move the overall market; it's the Federal Reserve Board... focus on the central banks, and focus on the movement of liquidity... most people in the market are looking for earnings and conventional measures. It's liquidity that moves markets.

quote: 59. If you want to mitigate risk effectively, you simply must acknowledge that stocks don't manage themselves. You're the manager, and it's up to you to protect your hard-earned capital.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 60. There's nothing new under the sun... things just repeat themselves over and over again. It's really identifying what has existed and what has happened in the past.
speaker: David Ryan

quote: 61. If you look at what the Fed did, the radical gamble they took to get inflation up 30 basis points from 1.7 to 2, it's, to me, sort of a risk-reward bet. You bet 1 to lose 40? And they lost.

quote: 62. This is the biggest redistribution of wealth from the middle class and the poor to the rich ever.

quote: 63. The key is to see things as they are—operating in the now—without seeing things as worse than they are out of fear, or better than they are out of greed.

speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 65. The road to success in the stock market is not a system or strategy; it's within you, and it will be realized only to the extent that you are able to control and direct your emotions as you encounter challenges.

quote: 66. I make my money on the few stocks a year that double and triple in price. The profits in those trades easily makes up for all the small losers.

quote: 67. Traders have to take their ego and throw it in a trash can when walking into the trading day because they are going to be wrong.

quote: 68. If you want to reap big gains in the market, make up your mind right now that you are going to separate trading from your ego. It's more important to make money than it is to be right.

quote: 69. Soros has taught me that when you have tremendous conviction on a trade, you have to go for the jugular. It takes courage to be a pig.

quote: 70. Bad news is sometimes the best buying opportunity life gives you.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 71. Amateurs think about how much money they can make. Professionals think about how much money they could lose.

quote: 72. Trade what you see, not what you think.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 73. If you're extremely confident, taking a loss doesn't bother you.

quote: 74. When I've looked at all the investors that have very large reputations — Warren Buffett, Carl Icahn, George Soros — they all only have one thing in common. It is to make large concentrated bets where they have a lot of conviction.

quote: 75. Stocks should be at a profit the first day you buy them.

quote: 76. Not losing big is the single most important factor for winning big. As a speculator, losing is not a choice, but how much you lose is.

quote: 77. Soros is the best loss taker I've ever seen. He doesn't care whether he wins or loses on a trade. If a trade doesn't work, he's confident enough about his ability to win on other trades that he can easily walk away from the position.

quote: 78. Looking at the biggest winners, we found that in many cases, the earnings had been on the table for a while.

quote: 80. You must adjust your risk as a function of potential reward.

quote: 81. I try not to get too complicated. I look at the daily Dow and that works but it's not foolproof.

quote: 82. Look at your own life. You can get so many stock ideas from just what you're buying. … From examining your own life, you can come up with unbelievable, great investing ideas.

quote: 84. There's no reason you should always be long. If you're sure a bear market is coming — go to cash.
speaker: Stanley Druckenmiller

quote: 85. Success in investing doesn't correlate with I.Q. once you're above the level of 125. Once you have ordinary intelligence, what you need is the temperament to control the urges that get other people into trouble in investing.

quote: 88. My favorite quote of all time is maybe Mark Twain: 'Put all your eggs in one basket and watch the basket carefully.' I tend to think that's what great investors do.

quote: 89. To have lasting success in the stock market, you must decide once and for all that it's more important to make money than to be right. Your ego must take a backseat.
speaker: Mark Minervini

quote: 90. Learn to buy weakness and sell strength, and not buy strength and sell weakness; because you're just going to continue to get whipsawed.
speaker: David Ryan
